A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LinguaMap study and complete 26-page manuscript, including appendices. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish identical page bodies, including equations, figures, tables and prompt examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual benchmark evaluations, layer-wise representation analyses, selective fine-tuning experiments and ablations in Sections 3–5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, representation analyses, fine-tuning comparisons and appendix ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: The logit-lens and hidden-state analyses, selective layer updates, frozen parameters and training objectives in Sections 4–5 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MMLU, MGSM and XQuAD coverage, language subsets, business-to-non-business evaluation and four prompting scenarios.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical model and comparator membership, including pre-fine-tuning, full-scope SFT and random selective SFT in Table 2 and the appendix.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, model configurations, training and validation splits, sample counts, decoding settings and training budgets are unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix A.3.

E4.justification: The layer-count and epoch ablations in Tables 10–11, prompting stress tests and post-fine-tuning representation analyses in Figures 4–5 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The mean and standard-deviation calculations in Equation 7 and existing plot uncertainty reporting are identical. Neither version adds run counts, seed information or statistical tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and 4–11, plotted results in Figures 2–5 and qualitative findings are unchanged. No results are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and their associated definitions and mathematical explanations are identical, including language consistency, representation similarity and selective-SFT objectives.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about multilingual failure modes, a three-phase layer structure and efficient selective fine-tuning for language control.

C2.justification: Mechanistic interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the token-level information lost through mean pooling and the remaining task-performance weakness under English distractors.

D1.justification: Section 7, Appendix A.3, Table 3 and the prompt templates retain identical reproducibility information, including optimizer, learning rate, hardware and inference settings. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list and statements positioning the contribution against prior research are identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds the header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026' and updates the arXiv stamp from v1 dated 27 January 2026 to v2 dated 22 March 2026. Body wording and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The running publication header and updated first-page arXiv stamp are the only visible changes. All six figures, eleven tables and appendix prompt boxes retain identical appearance and placement.

improvement.justification: The revision changes publication metadata only. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and substantive presentation remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
